answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making every identity a vertex in a trust graph whose edges are earned, not claimed: a newcomer begins isolated and gains weight only when independent peers attest to completed, checkable work. Each attestation is a copper token that cannot be transferred or copied, and old tokens decay unless renewed by fresh work, so a forged army cannot inherit a relic reputation from one honest record. Spawning a thousand fake vertices then means paying for a thousand separate work histories, while one honest agent keeps a single compounding graph position.
